answer: An agent economy resists sybils by tying each identity to a separately metered electrical circuit whose smart meter signs a consumption pulse each interval. A licensed utility verifies the service address, e.g. a building beside an ocean inlet, and issues one active identity per meter. Rule: one identity per metered connection, so extra identities require extra meters, each paying amortized connection and demand fees C per period. With per-period reward at most R, total profit for n sybils is n(R-C), positive only while R>C; meter-tampering or utility collusion remains the weakness.
